title: Godot Cache issues: overwriting AI changes
author: SirUseful626
selftext:
Hi, I am using Codex with Godot 4.7 and it works really well, but very often (like 30% of the time) I run into cache problems - or at least I think they are.

When Godot is running, the AI cannot freely change the scripts or files, Godot is holding a cached version and frequently overwrites the changes the AI is doing. I have to close all open scenes and all scripts to get the AI to do changes that actually apply, sometimes I even have to close the whole engine for it to work. This of course becomes tedious to constantly close and open Godot. Anyone else running into this issue?

comments.author: Heliaxx
comments.body: Yea it happend in some cases. A bit annoying but for me it doesn't really happen all that often so it's manageable. Haven't found any other solution than to just close the engine.

comments.author: PlaidWorld
comments.body:
1. 99% of the time this is a non issue.   
2. keep your ide and godot project open and it can reload files when you click on it every once in a while.  
3. Im pretty sure you can get he AI to kill the cache if you ask it and make it aware. Many things with AI you just need to ask for. 

I have been coding non stop with 2 different AI for 6 months and like 4+ sessions all working in the same code base and this really has not been an issue. 

I allow all the agents to run back ground tests / headless tests also.

replies.author: SirUseful626
replies.body:
I discussed this with ChatGPT for a long time and we have not found a solution. We are at the point that instead of them trying to fix the cache issue themselves (which they can do, but takes several minutes, sometimes they don't get that the code they just did is actually not there and then go on a scavengerhunt for even longer...) the AI prompts me to close the engine. I am using ZIVA as MCP, maybe that is what is causing problems....   
I have read around in Godot forums, it looks like this is an issue with certain code referencing subresources...

replies.body: I don’t use a mcp.  You really don’t need one with godot and  I’m not sure they actually help.  It also causes issues with being able to either have more then one agent work on a project or have more then one project open at a time.

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
You just minimize your godot editor and after a request is complete you just open godot windows again , it should auto update the cache , sometimes I work In godot while the agent works on something else 

As soon as I cntr shift to vscode and then back to godot , it adds the changes

replies.author: SirUseful626
replies.body: This is how it should work, and I have to pay closer to attention to this but I do not think it does work like that *all the time*. I come back to godot, did not touch it since the prompt, even reload the project as first thing, and the changes are gone. As if godot automatically overwrites stuff periodically. Now, maybe the AI ran the scene, which caused everything to save, which then overwrote old scripts over new ones. But it is not working properly right now. I am right now not using an external editor (VS Code) but willl try if that helps.

comments.author: _playlogic_
comments.body: The reason has to do with the .godot folder and your Agent making changes to files directly on disk and not doing it via Godot. When the editor is open it owns everything and use a EditorFileSystem process to update its cache. If the agent makes changes and that hasn’t rescanned the editor shows stale files. Unless your MCP is written poorly, then that’s is not the reason. This is the way Godot works and the agent needs to be aware of it to not get caught up. There are still times my custom tools still get caught by it, but I have skill docs that instruct my Agent how to deal with it

replies.author: SirUseful626
replies.body: and can you please tell me how to deal with it?
